concepts.title: Focal Length of Spherical Mirrors
concepts.definition: The focal length of a spherical mirror is the gap between its pole and the principal focus, and paraxial geometry fixes it at exactly half the radius of curvature.
concepts.key_idea: The focus sits midway between the pole and the centre of curvature, so halving R gives f for both mirror types.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph201.txt section 9.2.2 (small-angle derivation of f = R/2)

compute the focal length of a rear-view mirror whose curvature radius equals 2 m

solution_steps.explain: paraxial reflection puts the focus exactly halfway from the pole to the centre of curvature

concepts.title: Mirror Equation for Image Distance
concepts.definition: Object distance, image distance and focal length of any spherical mirror are locked together by one reciprocal relation, so two of the three quantities fix the third.
concepts.key_idea: With Cartesian signs a single formula handles concave and convex mirrors and every object position.
question_patterns: an object sits 27 cm from a concave mirror of focal length 18 cm; find the image distance
calculate where the image forms for an object 10 cm in front of a mirror with f = -7.5 cm
use the mirror formula to locate the image of a pin held 12 cm from a convex mirror of focal length 15 cm
what is the image position for an object placed beyond the focus of a concave mirror with focal length 15 cm
determine v from the mirror equation when u and f are given with proper signs
solve for the image distance of a candle 36 cm away from a mirror whose focal length is 18 cm

solution_steps.explain: the mirror equation works with reciprocals of the signed distances
the signed focal length converts to its reciprocal
rearranging 1/v + 1/u = 1/f gives 1/v = 1/f - 1/u
the reciprocal of 1/v is the signed image distance

concepts.title: Linear Magnification by a Mirror
concepts.definition: Linear magnification reports how many times taller the image is than the object; for a spherical mirror it equals minus the image distance divided by the object distance.
concepts.key_idea: A negative value flags an inverted real image while a positive one marks an erect virtual image.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph201.txt section 9.2.3 (Eq. 9.9, magnification after the mirror equation)
question_patterns: find the magnification when the image distance is -30 cm and the object distance is -10 cm
calculate the image-to-object size ratio for a mirror with v = 15 cm and u = -5 cm

an image forms at -12 cm while the object sits at -36 cm; compute m and state whether the image is erect
determine the magnification produced by a concave mirror for known object and image distances
how many times enlarged is the image when v and u are measured for a spherical mirror

solution_steps.action: divide image distance by object distance and flip the sign
solution_steps.explain: the signed magnification is minus v over u, so erect images get positive values

concepts.title: Refractive Index as a Speed Ratio
concepts.definition: A medium's refractive index compares how much slower light travels inside it than in vacuum; Snell's law expresses the same optical fact through the ratio of sines of the incidence and refraction angles.
concepts.key_idea: Optical density tracks the slowing of light, not mass density, so the index runs one and up for transparent media.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph201.txt section 9.3 (Snell's law Eq. 9.10 and the optical-density note)
question_patterns: light races through a medium at 2.25e8 m/s; find the refractive index

solution_steps.action: divide the vacuum speed by the medium speed
solution_steps.explain: the refractive index is exactly the factor by which the medium slows light

concepts.title: Apparent Depth in a Refracting Medium
concepts.definition: Seen from almost directly above, refraction lifts submerged objects toward the surface: the apparent depth comes out as the true depth split by the refractive index.
concepts.key_idea: The larger the refractive index, the shallower a tank bottom appears to a viewer above it.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph201.txt section 9.3 (apparent depth of a water-filled tank, near-normal viewing)
question_patterns: a coin lies on the bottom of an 80 cm deep water tank; find its apparent depth for near-normal viewing at index 1.33

solution_steps.action: split the true depth by the refractive index
solution_steps.explain: refraction bends rays at the surface so the bottom appears raised toward the viewer

concepts.title: Critical Angle and Total Internal Reflection
concepts.definition: For light leaving a denser medium, the critical angle is the incidence angle whose refracted ray just grazes the boundary at 90 degrees; past it, refraction fails and every ray turns back inside.
concepts.key_idea: Diamond's small critical angle near 24.4 degrees traps light by repeated total reflections, which makes the stone sparkle.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph201.txt section 9.4 (Eq. 9.12 and Table 9.1 of critical angles)
question_patterns: find the sine of the critical angle for glass of refractive index 1.5 facing air

a medium has refractive index 2.42; compute the sine of its critical angle with air
work out the grazing-angle sine for total internal reflection at a glass-air interface

solution_steps.action: take the reciprocal of the refractive index
solution_steps.explain: Snell's law with a 90 degree refraction angle gives sin(ic) = 1/n for the denser medium against air

concepts.title: Refraction at a Single Spherical Surface
concepts.definition: When rays cross one curved boundary between media of indices n1 and n2, the object and image distances connect through a relation that also carries the surface radius R.
concepts.key_idea: Applying this single-surface relation at both faces of a lens and adding the pieces builds the lens maker's formula.
question_patterns: light from a point source in air strikes a convex glass surface of radius 20 cm from 100 cm away; find the image position
use the spherical-surface relation to locate the image for n1 = 1, n2 = 1.5, R = 20 cm and u = -100 cm
a real object sits 50 cm from a curved interface of radius 10 cm between air and glass of index 1.5; calculate v
determine the image distance for refraction at one spherical boundary with given indices and radius
an object in air stands 25 cm from a glass surface of curvature radius 15 cm; where does its image form
compute v from the single-surface formula when u, R and both indices are supplied

solution_steps.explain: the surface strength is the index gap divided by the radius
the rearranged relation reads n2/v = (n2 - n1)/R + n1/u
the running sum holds n2/v, so the image distance is n2 over it

concepts.title: Thin Lens Equation
concepts.definition: For a thin lens the reciprocals of image distance and object distance combine into the reciprocal of the focal length, whatever the lens type or the nature of the image.
concepts.key_idea: Signs carry the physics: u is negative for a real object, f positive for a convex lens and negative for a concave one.
question_patterns: an object stands 14 cm from a concave lens of focal length 21 cm; find the image distance
calculate where a convex lens of focal length 12 cm forms the image of an object at 18 cm
what is v for a lens with f = 30 cm when the object sits 40 cm away
determine the image position from the thin lens formula given object distance and focal length with signs
a bulb is 40 cm from a convex lens of focal length 30 cm; locate the image
solve the lens equation for the image distance of a placed object

solution_steps.explain: the lens equation runs on reciprocal distances
the signed object distance joins as its reciprocal
rearranging 1/v - 1/u = 1/f gives 1/v = 1/f + 1/u
the reciprocal of 1/v is the signed image distance

concepts.title: Lens Maker's Formula
concepts.definition: The focal length a lensmaker can build in follows from the material index relative to the surroundings together with the two surface radii of curvature.
concepts.key_idea: The same glass immersed in water gains focal length because the relative index gap shrinks.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph201.txt section 9.5.2 (Eq. 9.21 and Example 9.7 part ii)
question_patterns: find the focal length of a double convex lens with radii 10 cm and -15 cm made of glass of index 1.5
calculate the focal length of an equiconvex lens of index 1.55 whose faces have 20 cm radius in air
what focal length does a lens of relative index 1.47 give when both surfaces curve at 20 cm
determine the focal length from the lens maker's relation for supplied radii and refractive index
a biconvex lens has equal 25 cm radii and index 1.5; compute its focal length in air
use the lens maker's formula to design a lens of wanted focal length from surface radii and index

solution_steps.explain: divide the lens index by the index of the surrounding medium
the shape factor is 1/R1 minus 1/R2 with signed radii
the formula multiplies the index gap by the shape factor to give 1/f
the reciprocal of 1/f is the focal length itself

concepts.title: Power of a Lens
concepts.definition: Lens power measures how strongly a lens converges or diverges light, quoted in dioptres once the focal length is written in metres.
concepts.key_idea: A shorter focal length means more power; converging lenses carry positive power and diverging ones negative.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph201.txt section 9.5.3 (Eq. 9.25, dioptre unit, Example 9.7 part i)
question_patterns: find the power of a lens whose focal length is 0.5 m

solution_steps.explain: power in dioptres equals one over the focal length expressed in metres

concepts.title: Combining Thin Lenses in Contact
concepts.definition: Thin lenses placed touching act as one lens whose inverse focal length is the sum of the individual inverse focal lengths.
concepts.key_idea: Powers add algebraically, so a convex and a concave lens in contact can partly cancel each other.
question_patterns: a convex lens of focal length 30 cm touches a concave lens of focal length 20 cm; find the combination's focal length
calculate the effective focal length when two thin lenses of 40 cm and 60 cm are placed in contact

compute the combined focal length for thin lenses held in contact

solution_steps.explain: each touching lens contributes additively to 1/f
the pair behaves as one lens with this focal length

concepts.title: Thin Prism Deviation
concepts.definition: A prism with a small refracting angle deflects a ray only slightly, and the deflection equals the relative-index gap multiplied by the prism angle.
concepts.key_idea: For thin prisms the minimum deviation grows in direct proportion to the refracting angle.
question_patterns: find the deviation produced by a thin prism of angle 5 degrees and refractive index 1.5
calculate the angle of deviation for a small-angle prism with A = 6 degrees made of glass of index 1.52

compute how much a thin prism bends light, given its index and refracting angle

solution_steps.action: scale the prism angle by the index gap
solution_steps.explain: the thin-prism limit multiplies (n - 1) by the small refracting angle

compute_steps.action: substitute the given values into the formula

concepts.title: Minimum Deviation Through a Prism
concepts.definition: At minimum deviation the ray inside the prism runs parallel to the base, incidence and emergence angles match, and the material index follows from the prism angle A with the minimum deviation Dm.
concepts.key_idea: Measuring A and Dm on the bench pins down the prism material's refractive index.
question_patterns: explain why the ray inside a prism travels parallel to its base at minimum deviation
show that at minimum deviation the incidence and emergence angles are equal
how do you extract a prism's refractive index from a measured minimum deviation
state the relation linking A, Dm and refractive index at minimum deviation
why does the deviation-versus-incidence curve dip to a single minimum
derive that each refraction angle equals half the prism angle at minimum deviation

solution_steps.explain: at the dip of the deviation curve, i equals e and r1 equals r2
r1 + r2 = A forces each refraction angle to A/2
sin i over sin r becomes sin((A + Dm)/2) over sin(A/2), which yields the index

concepts.title: Simple Microscope Magnification
concepts.definition: A single convex lens held near the eye serves as a magnifier; with the final image at the near point its magnifying power is one plus the near-point distance over the focal length.
concepts.key_idea: Placing the image at infinity trades a little magnification for relaxed viewing.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph201.txt section 9.7.1 (Eq. 9.39 and the f = 5 cm example)
question_patterns: find the magnifying power of a simple microscope of focal length 5 cm with the image at the near point

solution_steps.action: divide the near point by the focal length
solution_steps.explain: D is about 25 cm for a normal eye and f is the lens focal length
the near-point image adds the unity factor to the ratio

concepts.title: Compound Microscope Magnification
concepts.definition: A compound microscope chains a short-focus objective to an eyepiece; the objective magnifies linearly by L/fo while the eyepiece acts as a magnifier, so the two magnifications multiply.
concepts.key_idea: Both focal lengths must be short, and a longer tube length L raises the total magnification.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph201.txt section 9.7.1 (Eqs. 9.43-9.45 and the fo = 1 cm, fe = 2 cm example)

solution_steps.explain: the first image forms near the focal plane, so the linear factor is L/fo
the eyepiece behaves like a simple microscope with the image at infinity
the total magnifying power is the product of the stage magnifications

concepts.title: Telescope Magnifying Power
concepts.definition: An astronomical telescope magnifies angles rather than objects; in normal adjustment its magnifying power is the objective focal length divided by the eyepiece focal length.
concepts.key_idea: The tube length is the sum of the focal lengths, and a wide objective gathers more light and resolves finer detail.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph201.txt section 9.7.2 (Eq. 9.46 and the 144 cm / 6 cm telescope)
question_patterns: find the magnifying power of a telescope with a 144 cm objective and a 6 cm eyepiece
